data.one_liner: Multiplatform GPU compute for Dart and Flutter using WebGPU and Dawn.
data.what_it_does: Brings cross-platform GPU compute shaders to Dart and Flutter applications. It integrates WGSL and WebGPU directly utilizing a Dawn backend across mobile, desktop, and web.
use_when: You need to run high-performance compute shaders or AI-ML math models on the GPU across multiple platforms.
You want to process video frames or perform direct GPU buffer copies without CPU round-trips.
avoid_when: You are building a standard UI app that doesn't require low-level GPU acceleration.
You cannot handle complex native build setups involving CMake and Dawn.
strengths: Cross-platform support including Windows, Linux, macOS, Web, Android, and iOS.
Built-in persistent shader caching to mitigate compilation overhead.
Direct video frame import and interop for zero-copy GPU processing.
weaknesses: Dawn backend can take a long time to build and requires a recent version of CMake and Emscripten for web.
Experimental library with potential build friction on native platforms.
data.setup_notes: Requires CMake 3.22+ and Emscripten for web. Dawn is cloned and compiled automatically on first build, which may take time. Android requires a manually supplied shader cache directory.
